newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FORECAST-Bank/Portugal likely cut rates Friday.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Bank/Portugal likely cut rates Friday.

text.p: The Bank of Portugal should cut its repo rate by 10 to 20 basis points and lop up to 50 basis points off the drain rate, the level at which it absorbs market funds, on Friday for the start of the new commercial bank reserve period, analysts say.

The only real uncertainty was the state of the escudo which was losing ground against the mark on Friday. But analysts said that the movements in the Portuguese currency were due to the weakness of the peseta and the dollar and should not affect the Bank's decision.

Wednesday's discount rate cut by the Bank of Italy, the prime rate cut by Portugal's largest bank on Thursday and the wide rate gap with Spain all pointed in the direction of a move by the Bank of Portugal, analysts said.
The repo rate stands at 6.5 percent, against Spain's 6.0 percent, while the drain rate is 6.2 percent.

"I believe that the Bank will cut. It is possible that it cuts the repo by 10 basis points and the others (drain and emergency lending rate) by 25 basis points," said analyst Paula Carvalho of Banco Portugues de Investimento (BPI).
Isabel Cabral of Fincor said she expected the drain rate to be lowered by 30 basis points.
A third analyst, who asked not to be identified, saw cuts of 20 and 50 basis points, respectively in the repo and drain rates.
"The market has been waiting for a cut for a long time and even the Caixa de Depositos cut its prime rate. The Bank is going to have to cut," said Sergio Carvalho of Banco de Comercio & Industria.
The Caixa, Portugal's largest financial group, cut its prime rate by 25 basis points to 9.375 percent on Thursday.

Analysts saw the Bank limiting a reduction in the repo rate to 20 basis points because it was keeping a watchful eye on the evolution of prices for non-tradable goods, which edged up to five percent in December from 4.9 percent the previous month.
But there was no doubt that the financial markets were anticipating significant cuts over the coming months.

"Looking at the Forward Rate Agreements (FRA), especially the March +3, we can conclude that it is anticipating a strong cut in the Bank's intervention rates in the next two to three months," said analyst Martin Amaral Neto of Banco ESSI.
The FRA show that in March, short-term rates should be around 5.5 percent, in June 5.2 percent and in September 5.10 percent.

Analysts said that fact that the Bank of Portugal had been reported buying escudos at around 99.95 to the mark on Thursday should not change the outlook for a rate cut because the escudo eased in line with the peseta and the dollar.
They said that the intervention was only to smooth trading.
"I did not point to an inversion in the strengthening of the escudo. It was just a technical correction," Amaral Neto said.
